solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Preserved part of ship in protective coating

indicators.note: in tells us the ship's letters sit inside the coating word

parts.note: foil is a thin metal wrapping that protects food
SS is the abbreviation for steamship, prefixed to ships' names

explanation.surface: A conservator describes a bit of a ship kept safe under a protective layer.
explanation.definitionFit: A fossil is the remains of an ancient organism kept in rock, a part of it that has been preserved.

clue.text: Peculiar novel involving a thousand and one

indicators.note: involving means enclosing, so the novel word wraps round the other letters

parts.note: novel as an adjective means new, fresh
K stands for a thousand, as in 10K
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An odd novel tells of a thousand and one nights.
explanation.walkthrough: Novel reads as a book, but it is the adjective new.
explanation.definitionFit: Freakish means strange and abnormal, so peculiar.

clue.text: Deployed oars, protecting a religious leader's ongoing saga

indicators.note: protecting means surrounding, so the rearranged oars go round the other pieces
deployed means set out in a new arrangement, so oars is rearranged

parts.note: the Pope leads the Roman Catholic Church

explanation.surface: Rowers' oars are set out to guard a church leader on a long voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-running serial drama on TV or radio is an ongoing saga of everyday lives.

clue.text: Welshman's dentine depleted

definitions.note: Welshman's reads as Welshman is, a Welsh man's name

indicators.note: depleted means reduced, so the last letter is taken off

parts.note: ivory is the dentine of elephant tusks

explanation.surface: A Welsh man's teeth have worn away.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivor is a common Welsh male name, as for Ivor Novello.

clue.text: Serious outbreak of alarm about sea's return

indicators.note: about says the alarm word goes round the other piece

parts.note: panic is sudden alarm

indicators.note: return says the sea's short name is read backwards

parts.note: the Med is the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: Alarm spreads as a sea comes back, like a flood warning.
explanation.definitionFit: An epidemic spread over a whole country or the world is a serious outbreak of disease.

clue.text: A cheeky flower's opening

parts.note: pert means saucy or cheeky
a flower is something that flows, a river; the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A cheeky bloom starts to open its petals.
explanation.walkthrough: Flower means a river here, the thing that flows.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperture is a gap or hole, so an opening.

clue.text: Direct what comes out — something terribly dull

indicators.note: what comes out of a jumble is a new order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A command to steer whatever emerges, something tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: The British idiom is dull as ditchwater, meaning extremely boring.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagnant water in a ditch is the proverbial example of extreme dullness.

clue.text: Former empire raised without an inspirational phrase

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means read upwards, backwards
without means lacking, so the two letters are taken out

parts.note: the Ottoman Empire ruled from Turkey until 1922

explanation.surface: An old empire rose up without a stirring slogan.
explanation.definitionFit: A motto is a short saying adopted as a guiding principle or rallying cry.

clue.text: Audibly ageing, weep about unopened bill

indicators.note: about means round, so the weep word goes round the other piece

parts.note: to cry is to weep

indicators.note: unopened means without its opening, the first letter

parts.note: a bird's bill is its beak

explanation.surface: An old person weeps over a bill they haven't opened.
explanation.definitionFit: Creaky things make squeaking noises from age, so they sound old and worn.

clue.text: High on drug, showing guts

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed after

parts.note: a trip is a drug-induced high
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone high on drugs shows courage.
explanation.walkthrough: Guts suggests courage, but it means innards.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripe is the stomach lining of cattle eaten as food, so animal guts.

clue.text: Swept-back hair of solver and setter to inspire passion

indicators.note: hair swept back runs the other way, so the hair word is read backwards

parts.note: a mane is a long head of hair
what belongs to solver and setter together is ours, so OUR

explanation.surface: A slicked-back hairstyle shared by solver and setter is meant to stir up passion.
explanation.definitionFit: To enamour is to fill someone with love, so it is to inspire passion in them.

clue.text: Confer right to name

definitions.meaning: to give someone a right or claim to something
to give a book or film its title

explanation.surface: An official grants the right to choose a name.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to grant a right or claim and to give a title to a work.

clue.text: Bit of butter, something for a techie to twiddle?

definitions.text: something for a techie to twiddle?
definitions.meaning: a dial or control on a sound desk or machine

explanation.surface: A dab of butter set beside a gadget's controls, an odd pairing for a techie.
explanation.definitionFit: A small rounded lump of butter shares its word with the round control a technician turns.

clue.text: Stopgap repair about to plug bit of hose squashed flat

indicators.note: something that plugs a hole goes into it, so these pieces go inside the hosiery word

parts.note: hose is stockings and socks, and a sock is one item of it
a patch is a quick temporary repair
C is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: A quick fix is jammed into a leaky garden hose that has been squashed flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hose' suggests a garden hose, but here it is hosiery.
explanation.definitionFit: A spatchcocked bird is split down the back and pressed open, so it is cooked squashed flat.

clue.text: Fastest route from France to Hungary receiving gentle sign of approbation?

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so the two country letters go round the rest

parts.note: F is the international vehicle code for France
H is the international vehicle code for Hungary
a light touch is a gentle one
a pat on the back is a sign of approval

explanation.surface: Planning the quickest way across Europe from France to Hungary, with approval.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft's planned course is a flight path, meant as the quickest route through the air.

clue.text: Metallic fish in hovel

indicators.note: in places the fish inside the hovel word

parts.note: a sty is a pigsty, used of any filthy dwelling
an eel is a long snakelike fish

explanation.surface: A shiny fish is found in a squalid hut.
explanation.definitionFit: Steely describes something like steel in colour or hardness, so metal-like.

clue.text: Latitude for sign of life to incorporate deathshead

indicators.note: incorporate means take in, so the life sign word takes the extra letter inside

parts.note: breathing is the first sign that someone is alive
read as death's head: the head, or first letter, of death

explanation.surface: A grim scene where a sign of life must make room for a skull.
explanation.definitionFit: Latitude means scope or freedom, and breadth is the same sense of wide range.

clue.text: Agenda involving jar and last bit of hake fillet?

indicators.note: involving means enclosing, so the agenda word goes round the jar and letter

parts.note: an agenda is a list of to-dos
an urn is a large vase or jar

indicators.note: the last bit of hake is its final letter

explanation.surface: A cook's list includes a jar and the tail end of a piece of hake fillet.
explanation.walkthrough: The fish fillet in the surface is a red herring: the answer is a cut of beef.
explanation.definitionFit: Tournedos are small round steaks cut from beef fillet.

clue.text: Victualling-house in river getting on with flavouring

indicators.note: in puts the house word inside the river

parts.note: the Cam is the river through Cambridge
an inn provides food and drink

explanation.surface: An inn by the river serves food with spice.
explanation.definitionFit: Cinnamon is a spice from tree bark, used as flavouring.

clue.text: Rural friend eating mixed roast

indicators.note: eating means taking inside, so the friend word wraps round the rest

parts.note: a pal is a friend

indicators.note: mixed means jumbled, so the letters of roast are rearranged

explanation.surface: A country friend tucks into a mixed roast dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastoral means of the countryside and shepherding, so rural.

clue.text: A grain's fermented to produce booze

indicators.note: fermenting works and changes the stuff, so these letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Grain is fermented to make alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: Sangria is a Spanish drink of red wine and fruit, an example of booze.

clue.text: Unable to generate misty apparition

indicators.note: generate means produce something new, so the letters of unable make a new word

explanation.surface: Someone fails to conjure up a ghostly vision in the fog.
explanation.definitionFit: A nebula is a cloud of gas and dust in space, seen as a hazy glowing patch.

clue.text: Omar's blighted ash tree coming up

definitions.note: Omar's reads as Omar's surname, for the actor

indicators.note: blighted means ruined, so the letters of ash are rearranged
in a down clue coming up means read upwards

parts.note: a fir is a conifer tree

explanation.surface: Omar's ash tree is diseased but still growing.
explanation.definitionFit: Omar Sharif was the Egyptian actor of Lawrence of Arabia and Doctor Zhivago.

clue.text: Lacking talent, somewhat upset, exact penitence

indicators.note: upset says the hidden letters are read backwards
somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An untalented person, a bit put out, demands that others repent.
explanation.definitionFit: Inept means clumsy and unskilled, so without ability.

clue.text: Cheering 10 interrupting trial

indicators.note: interrupting means breaking into, so the number goes inside the trial word

parts.note: a court hearing is a trial of a case
the number 10 written as a word

explanation.surface: A cheering crowd counts to ten during a court case.
explanation.walkthrough: 10 looks like a reference to 10 across, but it is simply the number.
explanation.definitionFit: Heartening news is encouraging, so it cheers you up.

clue.text: A way to keep company, of course

indicators.note: to keep means to hold inside, so the street word holds the company

parts.note: St is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: A route for keeping company, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: Of course reads as naturally, but course is the racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascot is a racecourse in Berkshire, home of Royal Ascot.

clue.text: Insect's distinctive flavour going West

definitions.note: Insect's reads as insect is, the 's joining definition to wordplay

indicators.note: in an across clue going west means reading right to left

parts.note: a tang is a sharp distinctive taste

explanation.surface: An insect has a sharp taste and heads off westward.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnat is a small two-winged fly, one kind of insect.

clue.text: Chemist, one wanting one to treat the sick

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the one letter is taken out

parts.note: Marie Curie was the chemist who discovered radium
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A chemist is short of someone to look after the ill.
explanation.definitionFit: A remedy is something used to heal or treat illness.

clue.text: Demand return of lace knotted within border

indicators.note: within puts the knotted lace inside the border word

parts.note: a rim is an edge or border

indicators.note: knotting twists the lace up, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wants their lace back, now tied in knots around the edge of a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: To reclaim something is to ask for it back, to demand its return.

clue.text: Spoils start of play, left below

indicators.note: start of picks the first letter of play

parts.note: under means beneath, below

explanation.surface: A theatre review: the opening of the play leaves the rest beneath it and ruins things.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoils looks like a verb, ruins, but it is the noun meaning loot.
explanation.definitionFit: Plunder is goods taken by force, the spoils of a raid.

clue.text: Attractive female artwork

parts.note: an etching is a print made from an etched plate, a work of art

explanation.surface: A woman's picture is a lovely piece of art.
explanation.definitionFit: Fetching means charming in looks, the same as attractive.

clue.text: Withstand duplicitous character?

parts.note: an easel is a stand for a painter's canvas

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to hold out against a two-faced person.
explanation.walkthrough: Withstand must be split into with and stand to give the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A weasel is a sly, untrustworthy person, from the animal's reputation for cunning.
